title: Sun Yat-sen's birth chart
metaDescription: Sun Yat-sen's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.6° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.4° separates Mercury and Neptune from an exact trine; at that range thinking and imagination read as one mechanism. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 19.6° Scorpio — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Jupiter, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Mercury holds 10.8° Sagittarius, Venus holds 25.6° Sagittarius, Mars holds 27.8° Cancer — in the old shorthand, thought that arrives already in motion; attraction declared rather than implied; effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Nothing in the geometry sits closer than Mercury and Neptune: 0.4° from an exact trine. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, Mars opposition Jupiter at 0.9°, and Saturn opposition Pluto at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Moon opposes Uranus while both square Neptune. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. Venus makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks four placements here. The Moon in Capricorn at 11.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mercury in Sagittarius at 10.8° is in detriment; Mars in Cancer at 27.8° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Jupiter in Capricorn at 26.9° is in fall. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 4, earth 3, fire 3, and cardinal 5, fixed 3, mutable 2 across the modes. Water weights a chart toward the felt and the remembered — information that arrives as atmosphere before it arrives as words. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Capricorn for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 11.0°.
